description: One cell of an ArenaTableRow. The cell draws the cell box, which is the padding, the alignment and the mono or figure-ink treatment its column asks for. In card mode the cell draws the label and value pair or the full-width block instead. The cell shows whatever the consumer put in it. The cell's column config, its layout and its place in the grid's keyboard order come from ArenaTable and ArenaTableRow, and are members of no contract.

content.description: What the cell shows: a value, or one of Arena's own components, such as an ArenaBadge for a status or an ArenaButton for an action. The compound shape exists for this. The consumer instantiates one element per cell, so nothing here is per-item projection.

href.description: Present => the cell draws an <a> around its content, inside its own box, which is where HTML admits one. The member is the cell's rather than the row's. An anchor wrapping a row would break the row/cell structure the grid is made of, and may not contain the button a cell's own contract invites. The member carries the settled anchor convention rather than restating it, the same convention as ArenaCard.href, ArenaCommand.route, ArenaCrumb.href and ArenaSideNavItem.href. A primary click with no modifier is cancelled and reported through `navigate`, so a router owns it. Ctrl, meta, shift, alt, a middle click and a context menu stay the browser's and report nothing. The anchor is a tab stop of its own, which is the answer this table already gives for a control a consumer puts in a cell. The anchor is one Tab from the cell rather than a step-in the grid does not have. Inside a row carrying `interactive` the anchor wins and the row does not fire, because a press that lands on a control inside the row is never the row's. The anchor survives both shapes: below --bp-md the anchor is still an anchor and does not compete with the row's role="button", by the same predicate.

navigate.description: The cell's anchor was activated by the one activation a router owns, a primary click with no modifier. Arena has already cancelled the anchor's own navigation by the time the event fires. A modified click, a middle click and a context menu are the browser's and do not fire it at all. No payload, because the consumer wrote this element and already holds what it is about, the same shape as ArenaTableRow.click. The event is named `navigate` rather than click, because the cell has no other activation to report: with no `href` there is no anchor. An event that only ever fires for one member is named after what that member does.
